Love this game! Gameplay is smooth, replayable, controls feel nice as well. Was given this game by a friend, but definitely would have been willing to pay knowing how fun this game is.

There are a few select games in early access i have extremely high hopes for. After years of exploring half finished games and never seeing them live up to expectations or never even leave early access, my opinion on the category itself is extremely low. Once in a while however, a game stumbles into my recommended that catches my eye, Roboquest is such a game, the level of effort put into this game makes me hope that the aptly named RyseUp studios, can live up to that name and rise above the ever growing sea of trash early access seems to be.

Roboquest is a roguelite through and through, you start each run somewhat differently with new weapons and equipment to find and tailor your run to what you feel is strongest at the moment. The overall concept isnt anything new however, kill things to get things to upgrade things to kill the big thing and beat the thing then do the things all over again. But where Roboquest shines is in its refinement and presentation. 

Guns feel FANTASTIC, each gun looks and feels punchy, with the right amount of weight behind each gun to give the player the perfect amount of feedback. Shotguns punch through smaller enemies and chunk larger ones while the lighter SMGs are a bullet hose and quickly melt through both your magazine and the enemies health. Both fit a style of play and both are fun to use, whether or not they meet your DPS expectations depends on the mods you find, tailoring your ideal playstyle and what weapon class you want to use. 

The style of the game is a cutesy comic book style with very small cell shading undertones. Shooting weapons adds effects to pop up, like "BANG BANG" or "PEW PEW" depending on what gun your shooting and just adds to the colorful and comic book style. The story is told in comic book panels, and are actually really well made but might be unfinished or are meant to look that way, either is fine honestly. The only thing lacking is the detail of the actual levels, most surfaces are a flat color, and although i have no issue with it, its most apparent how baron the maps feel when you get to the 3rd stage and see a bunch of empty rooms.

The music is... Wow. If Mick Gordon had a younger brother who was into comic books and techno but kept all of his talent in making music, we'd get this. Noisecream is the maker of this actual noisecream, and even if you dont like the game, i strongly suggest listening to the OST and giving the soundtrack a buy here on steam. Doom taught me that music can add a whole new experience and pleasure to playing a game. Noisecream's performance skyrockets this games already great gameplay to what i can only describe as, indie doom.

Overall, I have very high expectations for Roboquest and the developers. They clearly put the effort into the base of the game with great feeling combat, movement, mechanics, and music. As long as they keep a steady amount of content and dont stray from what they refined here, we could be looking at the early stages of another to wash ashore the ever growing sea of early access trash and stand tall among the greats of gaming.

Simple but engaging first person roguelite with base-upgrading and a good variety of weapons. Definitely a strong 7/10 which can easily become an 8 or a 9 with additional class options and more things to spend your upgrade wrenches on. Would recommend.
